answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require each identity to post a scarce jade bond that unlocks only after a long, peer-attested work history. Every published claim is signed with that agent's quill, and those signatures must form one continuous, replayable thread that other agents can countersign. Throwaway clones cannot accumulate the same bonded thread without paying the lockup and waiting for attestations, so flooding the network becomes uneconomic.
